en: I bow to the Lord, the Sovereign whose form is Nirvāṇa, the all-pervading and omnipresent Brahman, whose very nature is the Veda. 1.
I worship my own Self—the space of consciousness, which is devoid of qualities, free from conceptual construction, desireless, and whose abode is the infinite sky. 2.
The formless one, whose root is the syllable Oṃ, the fourth state, the Lord who is beyond speech and knowledge, the Master of the Mountain. ||3||
I bow to Karāla, Mahākāla, Kāla, and Kṛpāla; to the abode of virtues, who has reached the further shore of saṃsāra. ||4||
Resembling the snowy mountain in its fair and profound luster, his body possessed the splendor and majesty of ten million Cupids.
The beautiful Gaṅgā flows as a surging river from his throbbing crown; on his neck, serpents coil around the shining crescent moon of his youthful brow.
With trembling earrings, beautiful eyebrows and eyes, and a broad, serene face—O Blue-throated One, you are compassionate.
I worship Śaṅkara, the beloved lord of all, who wears the skin of the king of beasts as his garment and a garland of severed heads. 8.
Fierce, supreme, bold, and the Lord of others; indivisible, unborn, and possessing the brilliance of ten million suns. ||9||
I worship Śūlapāṇi, the Lord of Bhavānī, who is accessible through devotion and who eradicates the three types of suffering. 10.
He who transcends time, the auspicious one, the bringer of the end of the aeon, the eternal bestower of joy upon the virtuous, the destroyer of the cities [of the demons]. 11.
O mass of consciousness and bliss, O remover of delusion, be gracious, be gracious, O Lord, O enemy of Manmatha! 12.
Until men in this world or the next worship the lotus feet of Umānātha, [they do not attain liberation]. 13.
There is as yet no happiness, no peace, and no destruction of torment; be gracious, O Lord, who dwells within all beings! 14.
I do not know yoga, nor indeed japa, nor worship; therefore, O Śambhu, I am always and at all times [devoted] to you. 15.
O Lord, O Āśīśa, O Śambhu, protect us who are afflicted and tormented by the flood of suffering consisting of birth and old age. 16.
This Rudrāṣṭaka has been proclaimed by a Brahmin for the gratification of Hara;
Śambhu is pleased with those men who recite it with devotion.
